summary: Gleidesk Renewables Acquisition Corp. (client, Buyer) is buying all outstanding stock of Tenein Rooftop Solar, Inc., a California residential and commercial rooftop solar installer, from Tenein Energy Holdings, LLC (Seller) for $48,500,000. The Stock Purchase Agreement was signed October 20, 2026 and has not yet closed. At Closing, Seller will also transfer certain Seller-owned installation vehicles, inverter and racking inventory and warehouse equipment used in the business, under a Form of Bill of Sale. The folder holds the signed SPA, the Form of Bill of Sale, Seller's Disclosure Schedule and a superseded September draft of the SPA. Four problems are planted. (1) The Bill of Sale pulls title claims under the indemnity cap, and the SPA's precedence clause lets it control for Transferred Assets. (2) The Bill of Sale chooses California law and forum, and the same precedence clause gives it effect. (3) The SPA makes Buyer's indemnity for 'Assumed Warranty Obligations' uncapped, and the Disclosure Schedule defines that term to include pre-Closing installations. (4) The renewal window for the Company's Fresno warehouse lease closed on October 2, 2026, before signing, even though SPA Section 6.4 obliges Seller to cause the renewal before Closing.

issues.label: Bill of Sale subjects title claims to the Cap despite the SPA carve-out
issues.description: SPA Section 9.4(b) excludes Fundamental Representations from the 10% Cap, and Section 4.6 (Title to Transferred Assets) is one of them. Section 4 of the Bill of Sale states that Seller's liability for breach of its title warranty to the Transferred Assets is 'subject to the Cap' in Section 9.4(a) of the Purchase Agreement. Normally the SPA would prevail. However, SPA Section 11.12 provides that the Bill of Sale controls as to the Transferred Assets. Read together, these clauses remove the carve-out for title losses on the vehicles, inventory and equipment. Buyer's recovery for defective title or undisclosed liens on those assets is then limited to $4,850,000.
issues.expected_finding: Because SPA Section 11.12 makes the Bill of Sale control as to Transferred Assets, Bill of Sale Section 4 overrides the Fundamental Representation carve-out in SPA Section 9.4(b) and caps Buyer's title claims at $4,850,000, so the Bill of Sale should be revised to state that title claims are uncapped consistent with Section 9.4(b) (or Section 11.12 amended so the SPA controls).

issues.label: Buyer's uncapped indemnity for Assumed Warranty Obligations reaches pre-Closing installations
issues.description: SPA Section 9.3(c) requires Buyer to indemnify Seller for all Losses arising from 'Assumed Warranty Obligations, as defined in Schedule 4.12 of the Disclosure Schedule'. SPA Section 9.4(d) provides that Buyer's obligations under Section 9.3(c) shall not be subject to the Cap or the Deductible. Schedule 4.12 of the Disclosure Schedule defines Assumed Warranty Obligations as all workmanship, roof-penetration and production warranty obligations on installations 'whether completed before or after the Closing Date'. The SPA incorporates this definition by reference, so the precedence clause does not resolve the point. The combined effect is that Buyer gives Seller an unlimited indemnity for pre-Closing workmanship defects. This conflicts with SPA Section 9.2, under which pre-Closing workmanship claims are meant to be Seller's capped responsibility. It also lets Seller pass its pre-Closing warranty exposure back to Buyer without limit.
detect_terms: shall not be subject to the Cap or the Deductible
issues.expected_finding: SPA Sections 9.3(c) and 9.4(d), read with the Schedule 4.12 definition that includes installations completed before Closing, expose Buyer to uncapped liability to Seller for pre-Closing workmanship warranty claims, so the definition should be limited to post-Closing installations and Buyer's indemnity made subject to a cap.

issues.label: Bill of Sale selects California law and forum, which controls under the precedence clause
issues.description: SPA Sections 11.8 and 11.9 select Delaware law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware Court of Chancery. Section 7 of the Bill of Sale states that it is governed by the laws of the State of California, with exclusive jurisdiction in the state courts located in Fresno County, California. Ordinarily the SPA would prevail. However, SPA Section 11.12 makes the Bill of Sale control as to the Transferred Assets. As a result, disputes over title to and transfer of the vehicles, inventory and equipment would be heard in California under California law, while related indemnity claims stay in Delaware. That splits a single dispute across two forums, risks inconsistent results and undermines the Delaware choice.
detect_terms: laws of the State of California
issues.expected_finding: Bill of Sale Section 7's California law and Fresno County forum conflict with SPA Sections 11.8–11.9 and, because SPA Section 11.12 lets the Bill of Sale control as to Transferred Assets, would split disputes between California and Delaware, so the Bill of Sale should be conformed to Delaware law and the Court of Chancery.

issues.label: Warehouse lease renewal window closed before signing
issues.description: Schedule 4.10(a) of the Disclosure Schedule describes the Company's Fresno warehouse lease with Pellucid Logistics Park LLC. The lease expires March 31, 2027, and the renewal option must be exercised by written notice no later than one hundred eighty (180) days before expiration. That deadline was October 2, 2026. The same schedule states that no renewal notice has been delivered. The SPA was signed October 20, 2026. SPA Section 6.4 records Buyer's position that Seller shall cause the Company to exercise the renewal option before Closing, but by signing that covenant could no longer be performed under the lease's terms. Because the lapse is disclosed against Section 4.10, Buyer has no rep-based indemnity claim. Buyer has not closed or otherwise accepted the lapse, so it can still act before Closing. Without action, the Company's main inventory and fleet facility could be lost shortly after Closing.
detect_terms: no later than one hundred eighty (180) days
no renewal notice has been delivered
issues.expected_finding: The renewal deadline under the Fresno warehouse lease (180 days before March 31, 2027, i.e. October 2, 2026) passed before the October 20, 2026 signing, so Seller cannot perform SPA Section 6.4 and Buyer should require, before Closing, a landlord-signed lease extension as a closing condition or a special indemnity for relocation costs.
